title: Muhyiddin's condition for new PM | Malaysiakini
text:
Muhyiddin's condition for new PM | Malaysiakini
Good morning, here's what you need to know today.
Muhyiddin's condition for new PM Umno vice-president Ismail Sabri Yaakob, the frontrunner to become the next prime minister, must not appoint leaders facing criminal charges as ministers if he comes to power. This is a condition imposed by outgoing prime minister Muhyiddin Yassin in exchange for Perikatan Nasional's support. The Yang di-Pertuan Agong concluded his verification exercise by interviewing all 114 MPs supporting Ismail. He wanted to ensure their support was not under duress . A total of 111 MPs are needed for a simple majority. If there are no doubts, the next step would be to swear in Ismail as the new prime minister but the ruler has indicated that it won't be as straightforward, unlike when he decided on the prime minister following the collapse of the Pakatan Harapan government in 2020. Among others, the palace wants the prime ministerial candidate to undergo a vote of confidence in Parliament and reconcile with opponents. More clarity is expected today after the Agong consults his fellow monarchs during a Conference of Rulers meeting, which His Majesty is convening to deal with the political crisis.
PN’s conditional support for Ismail does not count - Ambiga Support for any PM candidate must be unconditional. Hanipa pans Muhyiddin's anti-kleptocrat stance He claims the ex-PM's position is inconsistent. Opposition not invited to Istana Negara Only MPs in the majority were summoned.
Jostling for the DPM post With the post of the next prime minister set to go to Umno, Bersatu is expected to be compensated with the deputy prime minister position, leading to internal jostling among the party factions. The two frontrunners are Bersatu supreme council member Azmin Ali and Bersatu secretary-general Hamzah Zainuddin. A third name has emerged - Bersatu supreme council member Mohd Redzuan Md Yusof. His inner circle has been actively promoting his candidacy. While Azmin and Hamzah are more influential, they are not seen as being part of the "original" Bersatu. Hamzah defected from Umno and Azmin defected from PKR after the 14th general election, while Redzuan has been with Bersatu since its founding. However, it will be an uphill battle for Redzuan, who was sidelined during the previous Perikatan Nasional government.
'Even if PN returns to power, Bersatu faces bleak GE15' Bersatu is far smaller and younger than Umno. Kit Siang proposes Ismail-Anwar combo Bersatu's Rais Hussin makes a similar proposal. Suhakam wants institutional reforms Protect human rights, it tells the incoming govt.
Dine-in allowed in Klang Valley Muhyiddin Yassin spent his remaining days as the caretaker prime minister rolling out further relaxation of Covid-19 restrictions for fully vaccinated individuals. Beginning today, eateries in states still under Phase 1 of the National Recovery Plan will be allowed to offer dine-in services for fully vaccinated individuals. Other perks include more recreational and sporting activities including fishing, hiking, camping, cycling, golf and singles badminton or tennis matches. The Phase 1 states are Kedah, Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Negeri Sembilan, Malacca, Johor and Putrajaya. In justifying the relaxation, Muhyiddin touted that the rising vaccination rate is ensuring less severe Covid-19 infections. However, Health Ministry director-general Noor Hisham Abdullah said the relaxation was ultimately an economic, rather than a health consideration. Noor Hisham cautioned the people that it was not safe yet and that they should remain at home, even if they are allowed to go to more places.
